decision: A private per-service Snapshots registry holds at most128 exact new-job tasks, maximum2 worker threads, no persistent idle workers. Enqueue returns without waiting for network or disk. Each task owns job snapshot/current cancel Arc and an optional native ProfileReceiver capability; deduplicate only exact job ID within that registry. A completed task is not automatically retried.

Register only after new encoded/raw job state and immutable owner proof are durable, and only for pending jobs actually created by download_batch, never reused/loaded/retried historical jobs. New download UUID directories may be created by the optional task under safe-path and current-owner guards. Existing files are never rewritten or deleted.

Tasks expire before starting if queued longer than15seconds. Existing anonymous lookup limits remain: YouTube5seconds; SOOP VOD metadata20seconds, station12seconds, image4seconds, at most36seconds sequential work. Check cancellation before and after every phase. No hard interruption of an already-running bounded HTTP call is claimed. Existing public identity/raster/host/redirect limits and no-cookie rules remain; no new media, account, or renderer URL source.

Before lookup and before save require exact current job/request/ref/root/created/broadcast identity, same cancel Arc, active job with no library, noncancelled token and nonshutting-down service. A recording capability contains Weak official receiver and exact RecordingOwner, verifies receiver ID/ref/broadcast/current recording job and immutable proof owner. Acquire recording mutex before service state mutex, matching existing begin; never hold either during network work.

Use existing Profile::from_data_url and create_new Profile::save once. Final small bounded file write/sync remains under current-owner commit gates so cancel/delete/replacement cannot win then receive a stale save; this is not network blocking or a media completion dependency. A dedicated receiver profile_commit mutex serializes closed.store with optional commit; snapshot order is profile_commit then recording then service.state, close takes existing YouTube binding then profile_commit and never recording/state. Failed lookup/storage/spawn is optional and never changes video/chat job result or retries media. Preserve incomplete sidecar on IO failure rather than overwrite it.

Expose queued/running task IDs through existing service active_ids so shutdown observes bounded work even after a media owner exits. Reuse platform-media:job_id and deduplicate against the media task to avoid double counting; an optional lookup still draining after media completion remains counted as background work until its bounded return. Shutdown already sets current job cancel tokens/state; queued tasks skip, running work rechecks before writing. A profile worker cannot remove a job token, mark a job completed/failed, or retain a native viewer lease.

Profile is an immutable observation acquired during this new job, not a backdated historical channel picture. If capture stops before it can commit, leave it absent; existing explicitly current-photo library fallback may still display a current picture. No claims of guaranteed portrait availability when public metadata is absent or task limits prevent work.

Ordinary cfg(test) new-job registration uses a no-network loader; private deterministic tests explicitly inject a synthetic loader. This test-only seam neither adds a production option nor changes production public lookup. Worker loop catches per-task panic, removes active registration, and releases worker reservations; spawn failure drops optional queued work if no worker remains. Registry lock is always released before receiver/service locks.
